Subject: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi Tom / Samantha,

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can get the on-prem air-gapped qualification moving:

Call recap (high level):
- LegacyBank is evaluating a fully air-gapped Private deployment (no direct internet egress).
- Primary workloads: customer support triage & PII redaction at 1k-2k requests/day, peak concurrent inference ~40 sessions.
- Preference for on-prem appliance or VPC-connected blades in LegacyBank data centers; must support offline upgrades and signed images.

Requested follow-ups / open items:
1) Hardware footprint: rack count, rack unit constraints, available PDUs, and per-rack power budget (amps/volts). We attached a short workbook to record specs (redwood_onprem_hw_workbook.xlsx).
2) Network topology: confirm whether an isolated jump host is acceptable for administrative pulls vs fully sealed air gap. We attached our baseline network_requirements.pdf.
3) Offline upgrade process: do you require USB / air-gapped media delivery only, or is a removable drive + validated signature acceptable? Any signing requirements (internal KMS/HSM)?
4) Maintenance windows & on-call: preferred cadence for quarterly security updates and emergency patching.
5) Procurement timeline: point of contact in procurement for SOW/PO and any procurement constraints.

Next steps we propose:
- Please fill the workbook with hardware/power details and return to me (cc Dev) by EOD Friday 3/24.
- Dev to run a short technical validation once we have the workbook answers — 30\u201345 minutes.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_hw_workbook.xlsx (workbook), network_requirements.pdf

If helpful I can send a short architecture diagram and an example offline upgrade runbook prior to the tech call.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers / clarifications from our side:
- Rack/power: We have 2 racks available in DC-3, each 42U. Power per rack: 3x 20A PDUs, redundant A/B feed available.
- Network: We cannot permit any outbound internet from the cluster. We can support a bastion/jump host on an isolated management VLAN that has strict ACLs and is physically isolated from corporate internet.
- Offline upgrades: We prefer signed images delivered on removable NVMe or encrypted USB. We do have an internal HSM for signing images; important that images be verifiable against our signing key.
- Maintenance: Quarterly maintenance windows are preferred; emergency patching requires a 24h notice and approval from SecOps.
- Procurement: looping in procurement (procurement@legacybank.com) here — expected SOW review after technical validation.

Two questions for Redwood:
1) Do you support image signing with customer-owned keys/HSM?
2) For hardware recommendations, we prefer guidance on GPU models that support ECC and have NVMe scratch.

Also attaching an internal network diagram (see attachment) — I'll send that separately if helpful.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Tom / Samantha,

Thanks for the quick answers — helpful. A few technical clarifications based on your items:

1) Image signing / HSM
- Yes, we support validating images signed with customer-owned keys. Our offline upgrade flow supports signature verification at install time; we can integrate with an HSM-backed signing process or verify signatures against a provided public key. Please let me know the signing algorithm and key format you use (RSA-2048/4096 or ECDSA).

2) Hardware guidance (recommendation for your workload ~40 concurrent sessions):
- GPU: 4 x A30 or 4 x H100 (depending on model size & throughput targets). H100s give better inference headroom but require higher power and cooling.
- CPU: 2 x 24-core server-class CPUs.
- Memory: 512GB DDR4 ECC.
- Storage: 2 x 2TB NVMe for model artifacts + 4 x 8TB NVMe for cache and local datasets (RAID/redundancy per your ops practice).
- Networking: 25/100GbE uplinks as available; management VLAN for the bastion host.

3) Offline upgrade options:
- Option A (fully air-gapped): we provide signed image tarballs and a verified installer that runs locally from removable NVMe. You verify signatures locally; installer logs written to local audit store.
- Option B (controlled jump host): jump host pulls updates from a sealed internal repo (accessible only from bastion); bastion then distributes to cluster.

4) On-call / emergency patching
- We can provide an offline playbook for emergency patching that includes signed hotfix images and a verification checklist. If you need an SLA for on-site support, we can include an SOW addendum for onsite engineers during upgrades.

Next step: if you confirm you can share the completed workbook by EOD 3/24, I'll prepare a short tech validation plan (30\u201345m) and a proposed hardware SKU list (incl. cooling & PDU requirements). I can share an example offline upgrade runbook ahead of the call.

Regards,
